paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness plugin: use your own local OpenCode CLI's models (all your OpenCode providers) insi
de DSH, the way T3 Code does
# dsh-plugin-opencode-local
## Why this exists
I wanted to use OpenCode's models in DeepSeek Harness through the OpenCode CLI installed on my own m
achine, the way T3 Code does. I couldn't find a DeepSeek Harness plugin that did that, so I built th
the way T3 Code does. I couldn't find a DeepSeek Harness plugin that did that, so I built this one.
## What it does
A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that adds an **OpenCode (local)** model provider. Every request is s
erved by your own installed OpenCode, the same way T3 Code does it: one `opencode serve` on `127.0.0
.1`, started from your install with your own login and config, driven only through OpenCode's offici
d from your install with your own login and config, driven only through OpenCode's official clients.
- Your models: every model of every provider you are signed in to in OpenCode, plus OpenCode's own f

ree models, with OpenCode's `provider/model` ids.
- Your login: the plugin never reads, copies or fo

rwards `auth.json` or any credential. OpenCode uses its own.
- Your machine: all model traffic goes
through your `opencode` process. The plugin makes no calls to `opencode.ai` or any other host, uses
no proxies, and sets no custom headers or user agent.
## Compatibility

| DeepSeek Harness | 0.2.x (tested on 0.2.1-rc.5) |
| DSH profiles | Desktop app and CLI/headless pr

ofiles |
| OpenCode | 1.14.19 or newer, including 2.x |
| Platforms | Windows (tested end to end), L

inux (CI); macOS should work but is untested |
| Node | 22.19 or newer (DSH ships its own) |
Restricted OpenCode tools (shell, file edits, web fetch) go through DSH's approval prompt; see Permi
enCode tools (shell, file edits, web fetch) go through DSH's approval prompt; see Permission policy.

1. Install OpenCode and check it runs:

2. Add the plugin to DSH.
- **DSH desktop app:** open the plugin manager and add `dsh-plugin-opencod

e-local`.
- **DSH CLI:**
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Use the name of your own profile in place of `web`, for example `desktop` or `headless`.
To try an unreleased version, build it (`npm ci && npm pack`) and add the `.tgz` file instead.
3. Restart DSH, open the model picker, and choose a model under **OpenCode (local)**.
The provider also shows up in **Settings → Models**, where **Edit** opens its settings:
The plugin has no install scripts and downloads nothing. If `opencode` can't be found, the first req
uest tells you how to install it or where to point `binaryPath`.
## Settings
In DSH under Settings → Models → OpenCode (local), or in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` under `ds
h-plugin-opencode-local`.
| Setting | Default | What it does |

| `binaryPath` | `opencode` | Path or PATH name of your `opencode` executable. |
| `serverUrl` | emp
ty | Attach to an `opencode serve` you already run (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:4096`) instead of startin

g one. |
| `serverPassword` | empty | That server's password (`OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD` for 1.x, `O

PENCODE_PASSWORD` for 2.x). |
| `cwd` | empty | Working directory for OpenCode sessions. Empty uses

the DSH conversation's working directory. |
| `allowRestrictedTools` | `false` | Allow the restricte

d tools (below) without asking. |
| `askForApproval` | `true` | Ask in DSH's approval prompt before

a restricted tool runs. When off, they're rejected. |
| `requestTimeoutMs` | `1800000` | Upper bound

for one turn, in ms. `0` means no limit. |
| `modelRefreshSeconds` | `300` | How often the model li

st is re-read from OpenCode. |
| `showToolActivity` | `true` | Show OpenCode's tool calls as short l

ines in the reply. |
| `localSessionTitles` | `true` | Make DSH session titles locally instead of sp
ending a model request on them. |
## How it works
- **One shared server.** On the first request the plugin runs `opencode --version`, then `opencode s
erve --hostname=127.0.0.1 --port=<free port>` with your full environment and a new random password.
It waits for the "listening" line and checks `/global/health` (1.x) or `/api/info` (2.x). If the ser
ver crashes it is restarted with backoff. When DSH stops or the plugin is disabled, the whole proces

s group (or process tree on Windows) is killed.
- **Sessions.** Each DSH conversation gets its own O
penCode session in the conversation's working directory. Only the new message is sent each turn. If
the DSH history no longer matches what OpenCode has seen (DSH restarted, a message was edited, the c
onversation was compacted, or a turn failed), a new session is created and seeded with the DSH trans

cript.
- **Streaming.** Text, reasoning, tool activity and token usage stream into DSH. Stopping a r

eply in DSH aborts the OpenCode run.
- **Images.** png, jpeg, gif and webp up to 20 MB are sent to m
odels that accept images.
## Permission policy
The same policy as T3 Code's default (non full-access) mode:
- **Always allowed:** `question`, `read`, `glob`, `grep`, `lsp`, `todowrite`, `task`, `skill`. Readi

ng `.env` files still asks; `.env.example` doesn't.
- **Restricted:** `bash` (`shell` in 2.x), `edit
`, `webfetch`, `websearch`, `codesearch`, `external_directory`, `doom_loop`, and anything not listed
, `webfetch`, `websearch`, `codesearch`, `external_directory`, `doom_loop`, and anything not listed.
Restricted tools are configured as `ask`, never `deny`. (A `deny` rule makes OpenCode's free tier re
fuse requests with `FreeTierError`.) When OpenCode asks:

1. if `allowRestrictedTools` is on, it's allowed once;
2. otherwise, if DSH's approval prompt is ava

ilable and `askForApproval` is on, you decide;
3. otherwise it's rejected, and the model gets a mess
age saying the tool was not granted and not to retry.
For 1.x the policy is passed in `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT` (your own `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT`, if se
t, is kept and only its `permission` key replaced). For 2.x it's set as session permission rules. Th
e plugin never uses `--auto` or allow-all.
OpenCode questions (the `question` tool) can't be shown in DSH, so they're declined and the model co
ntinues without an answer.
## Errors
OpenCode's error message is shown as is.
| OpenCode | DSH failure |
| HTTP 429, `FreeUsageLimitError` | `RATE_LIMIT`. The plugin doesn't retry it; wait and try again. |

| HTTP 401/403, `FreeTierError`, `ProviderAuthError` | `AUTH` |
